text: Let $λ\neq 0$ be a real number. Let $α,β$ be the roots of the equation $14x^{2}-31x+3λ=0$ and $α,γ$ be the roots of the equation $35x^{2}-53x+4λ=0$. Then $\frac{3α}{β}$ and $\frac{4α}{γ}$ are the roots of the equation
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$14x^{2}-31x+3λ=0$

$\begin{array}{l} α+β=\dfrac{31}{14}\ldots .(1)\text{and}αβ=\dfrac{3λ}{14}...(2) \\  \\ 35x^{2}-53x+4λ=0 \\  \\ α+γ=\dfrac{53}{35}\ldots (3)\text{and}αγ=\dfrac{4λ}{35}\ldots (4) \\  \\ \dfrac{(2)}{(4)}\Rightarrow \dfrac{β}{γ}=\dfrac{3\times 35}{4\times 14}=\dfrac{15}{8}\Rightarrow β=\dfrac{15}{8}γ \end{array}$

(1) $-(3)\Rightarrow β-γ=\frac{31}{14}-\frac{53}{35}=\frac{155-106}{70}=\frac{7}{10}$

$\frac{15}{8}γ-γ=\frac{7}{10}\Rightarrow γ=\frac{4}{5}$

$\Rightarrow β=\frac{15}{8}\times \frac{4}{5}=\frac{3}{2}$

$\Rightarrow α=\frac{31}{14}-β=\frac{31}{14}-\frac{3}{2}=\frac{5}{7}$

$\Rightarrow λ=\frac{14}{3}αβ=\frac{14}{3}\times \frac{5}{7}\times \frac{3}{2}=5$

so, sum of roots $\frac{3α}{β}+\frac{4α}{γ}=\left (\frac{3αγ+4αβ}{βγ}\right )$

$\begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{\left (3\times \frac{4λ}{35}+4\times \frac{3λ}{14}\right )}{βγ}=\dfrac{12λ(14+35)}{14\times 35βγ} \\  \\ =\dfrac{49\times 12\times 5}{490\times \frac{3}{2}\times \frac{4}{5}}=5 \end{array}$

Product of roots

$=\frac{3α}{β}\times \frac{4α}{γ}=\frac{12α^{2}}{βγ}=\frac{12\times \frac{25}{49}}{\frac{3}{2}\times \frac{4}{5}}=\frac{250}{49}$

So, required equation is $x^{2}-5x+\frac{250}{49}=0$

$\Rightarrow 49\mathrm{x}^{2}-245\mathrm{x}+250=0$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Let $B$ and $C$ be the two points on the line $y+x=0$ such that $B$ and $C$ are symmetric with respect to the origin. Suppose $A$ is a point on $y-2x=2$ such that $△ABC$ is an equilateral triangle. Then, the area of the $△ABC$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Origin $(O)$ is mid-point of $BC(x+y=0)$.

$A$ lies on perpendicular bisector of $BC$, which is $x-y=0$

A is point of intersection of $x-y=0$ and $y-2x=2$

$\therefore A\equiv (-2,-2)$

Let $h=AO=\frac{-2-2}{\sqrt{1^{2}+1^{2}}}=2\sqrt{2}$

$\text{Area}=\frac{h^{2}}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{8}{\sqrt{3}}$

text: Three rotten apples are mixed accidently with seven good apples and four apples are drawn one by one without replacement. Let the random variable X denote the number of rotten apples. If $μ$ and $σ^{2}$ represent mean and variance of X, respectively, then $10(μ^{2}+σ^{2})$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Drawing 4 apples one by one without replacement gives the same distribution of the number of rotten apples as drawing 4 together from 10 (3 rotten, 7 good), so

$P(X=k)=\frac{\left (3k\right )\left (7 4-k\right )}{\left (10 4\right )},\left (10 4\right )=210$

$P(X=0)=\dfrac{35}{210}$, $P(X=1)=\dfrac{3\times 35}{210}=\dfrac{105}{210}$, $P(X=2)=\dfrac{3\times 21}{210}=\dfrac{63}{210}$, $P(X=3)=\dfrac{1\times 7}{210}=\dfrac{7}{210}$.

$μ=\sum kP(X=k)=\frac{0+105+126+21}{210}=\frac{252}{210}=\frac{6}{5}$

$E(X^{2})=\sum k^{2}P(X=k)=\frac{0+105+252+63}{210}=\frac{420}{210}=2$

Since $σ^{2}=E(X^{2})-μ^{2}$, $μ^{2}+σ^{2}=E(X^{2})=2$, and $10(μ^{2}+σ^{2})=20$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Let $f(θ)=3\left (\sin ^{4}\left (\frac{3π}{2}-θ\right )+\sin ^{4}(3π+θ)\right )-2(1-\sin ^{2}2θ)$ and $S=\left \{θ\in [0,π]:f^{'}(θ)=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right \}$. If $4β=\sum\limits _{θ\in S}θ$, then $f(β)$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(θ)=3\left (\sin ^{4}\left (\frac{3π}{2}-θ\right )+\sin ^{4}(3π+θ)\right )-2\left (1-\sin ^{2}2θ\right )$

 $S=\left \{θ\in [0,π]:f^{'}(θ)=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right \}$ 

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(θ)=3\left (\cos ^{4}θ+\sin ^{4}θ\right )-2\cos ^{2}2θ$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(θ)=3\left (1-\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{2}2θ\right )-2\cos ^{2}2θ$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(θ)=3-\frac{3}{2}\sin ^{2}2θ-2\cos ^{2}2θ$

 $=\frac{3}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\cos ^{2}2θ=\frac{3}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{1+\cos 4θ}{2}\right )$

$f(θ)=\frac{5}{4}-\frac{\cos 4θ}{4}$

$f^{'}(θ)=\sin 4θ$

$\Rightarrow f^{'}(θ)=\sin 4θ=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow 4θ=\mathrm{n}π+(-1)^{\mathrm{n}}\frac{π}{3}$

$\Rightarrow θ=\frac{\mathrm{n}π}{4}+(-1)^{\mathrm{n}}\frac{π}{12}$ 

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow θ=\dfrac{π}{12},\left (\dfrac{π}{4}-\dfrac{π}{12}\right ),\left (\dfrac{π}{2}+\dfrac{π}{12}\right ),\left (\dfrac{3π}{4}-\dfrac{π}{12}\right ) \\  \\ \Rightarrow 4β=\dfrac{π}{4}+\dfrac{π}{2}+\dfrac{3π}{4}=\dfrac{3π}{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow β=\dfrac{3π}{8}\Rightarrow f(β)=\dfrac{5}{4}-\dfrac{\cos \frac{3π}{2}}{4}=\dfrac{5}{4} \end{array}$

text: Fifteen football players of a club-team are given 15 T-shirts with their names written on the backside. If the players pick up the T-shirts randomly, then the probability that at least 3 players pick the correct T-shirt is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Required probability $=1-\frac{D_{(15)}+{}^{15}C_{1}\cdot D_{(14)}+{}^{15}C_{2}D_{(13)}}{15!}$

Taking $\mathrm{D}_{(15)}$ as $\frac{15!}{e}$

$\mathrm{D}_{(14)}$ as $\frac{14\text{!}}{e}$

$\mathrm{D}_{(13)}$ as $\frac{13\text{!}}{e}$

$\text{We get,}\text{Required probability}=1-\left (\frac{\frac{15!}{e}+15\cdot \frac{14!}{e}+\frac{15\times 14}{2}\times \frac{13!}{e}}{15!}\right )$

$=1-\left (\frac{1}{e}+\frac{1}{e}+\frac{1}{2e}\right )=1-\frac{5}{2e}\approx .08$

text: Let the tangents at the points $A(4,-11)$ and $B(8,-5)$ on the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-3x+10y-15=0$, intersect at the point $C$. Then the radius of the circle, whose centre is $C$ and the line joining $A$ and $B$ is its tangent, is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Equation of AB :

$y-(-5)=\frac{-5+11}{8-4}(x-8)$

$\Rightarrow y+5=\frac{3}{2}(x-8)$

$\Rightarrow 2y+10=3x-24$

$\Rightarrow 3x-2y-34=0$ .... (1)

Also AB is chord of contact. And we know equation of chord of contact to a circle is $T=0$

$\Rightarrow xh+yk-\frac{3}{2}(x+h)+5(y+k)-15=0$

$\Rightarrow x\left (h-\frac{3}{2}\right )+y(k+5)+\left (-\frac{3}{2}h+5k-15\right )=0$ .... (2)

Comparing equation (1) and (2), we get

$\frac{h-\frac{3}{2}}{3}=\frac{k+5}{-2}=\frac{-\frac{3}{2}h+5k-15}{-34}$

$\therefore$ $-2h+3=3k+15$

$\Rightarrow 3k+2h=-12$ ..... (3)

and

$17(k+5)=-\frac{3}{2}h+5k-15$

$\Rightarrow 12k+\frac{3}{2}h+100=0$

$\Rightarrow 3h+24k=-200$ ..... (4)

Solving (3) and (4), we get

$h=8$ and $k=-\frac{28}{3}$

$\therefore$ Point C is $\left (8,-\frac{28}{3}\right )$

Now radius of the circle whose centre is at C and tangent is AB is

$=\left |\frac{3(8)-2\left (-\frac{28}{3}\right )-34}{\sqrt{3^{2}+2^{2}}}\right |$

$=\left |\frac{26}{3\sqrt{13}}\right |$

$=\frac{2\sqrt{13}}{3}$

 satisfies $f(x)=x+\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\sin (x+y)f(y)dy$. then $(a+b)$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=x+\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}(\sin x\cos y+\cos x\sin y)f(y)dy$

$f(x)=x+\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}((\cos yf(y)dy)\sin x+(\sin yf(y)dy)\cos x)....(1)$

On comparing with

$f(x)=x+\frac{a}{π^{2}-4}\sin x+\frac{b}{π^{2}-4}\cos x,x\in \mathrm{ℝ}$ then

$\Rightarrow \frac{a}{π^{2}-4}=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\cos yf(y)dy....(2)$

$\Rightarrow \frac{b}{π^{2}-4}=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\sin yf(y)dy....(3)$

Add (2) and (3)

$\frac{a+b}{π^{2}-4}=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}(\sin y+\cos y)f(y)dy....(4)$

$\frac{a+b}{π^{2}-4}=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}(\sin y+\cos y)f\left (\frac{π}{2}-y\right )dy....(5)$

Add (4) and (5)

$\frac{2(a+b)}{π^{2}-4}=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}(\sin y+\cos y)\left (\frac{π}{2}+\frac{(a+b)}{π^{2}-4}(\sin y+\cos y)\right )dy$

$=π+\frac{a+b}{π^{2}-4}\left (\frac{π}{2}+1\right )$

$(a+b)=-2π(π+2)$

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

text:
For two non-zero complex numbers $z_{1}$ and $z_{2}$, if $\mathrm{Re}(z_{1}z_{2})=0$ and $\mathrm{Re}(z_{1}+z_{2})=0$, then which of the following are possible?

A. $\mathrm{Im}(z_{1})>0$ and $\mathrm{Im}(z_{2})>0$

B. $\mathrm{Im}(z_{1})<0$ and $\mathrm{Im}(z_{2})>0$

C. $\mathrm{Im}(z_{1})>0$ and $\mathrm{Im}(z_{2})<0$

D. $\mathrm{Im}(z_{1})<0$ and $\mathrm{Im}(z_{2})<0$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, $z_{1}=x_{1}+iy_{1}$

and $z_{2}=x_{2}+iy_{2}$

$\therefore$ $z_{1}z_{2}=x_{1}x_{2}-y_{1}y_{2}+i(x_{1}y_{2}+x_{2}y_{1})$

Given, $\mathrm{Re}(z_{1}+z_{2})=0$

$\Rightarrow x_{1}+x_{2}=0$ ...... (1)

also given, $\mathrm{Re}(z_{1}z_{2})=0$

$\Rightarrow x_{1}x_{2}-y_{1}y_{2}=0$

$\Rightarrow x_{1}x_{2}=y_{1}y_{2}$

$\Rightarrow y_{1}y_{2}=-x_{1}^{2}$ [$\because$ $x_{2}=-x_{1}$]

So, multiplication of imaginary part's of $z_{1}$ and $z_{2}$ is negative. It means sign of $y_{1}$ and $y_{2}$ are opposite of each other.

$\therefore$ B and C are correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Let $y=f(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $y(x+1)dx-x^{2}dy=0,y(1)=e$. Then $\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}f(x)$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$y(x+1)dx-x^{2}dy=0$

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{x+1}{x^{2}}\right )dx=\frac{dy}{y}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{x}dx+\frac{dx}{x^{2}}=\frac{dy}{y}$

Integrating both sides, we get

$\int \frac{dx}{x}+\int \frac{dx}{x^{2}}=\int \frac{dy}{y}$

$\Rightarrow \ln |x|-\frac{1}{x}=\ln |y|+C$ ..... (1)

Given $y(1)=e$

$\therefore$ $x=1$ and $y=e$

Putting value of x and y in equation (1), we get

$\ln |1|-\frac{1}{1}=\ln |e|+C$

$\Rightarrow 0-1=1+C$

$\Rightarrow C=-2$

$\therefore$ Equation (1) becomes,

$\ln |x|-\frac{1}{x}=\ln |y|-2$

$\Rightarrow \ln |y|=\ln |x|-\frac{1}{x}+2$

$\Rightarrow y=e^{\ln |x|}.e^{2-\frac{1}{x}}$

$\Rightarrow y=x.e^{2-\frac{1}{x}}$

Now,

$\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}y$

$=\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}\left (x.\quad e^{2-\frac{1}{x}}\right )$

$=0.\qquad e^{-\infty }$

$=0$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Let $f:R\to R$ be a function such that $f(x)=\frac{x^{2}+2x+1}{x^{2}+1}$. Then
options: $f(x)$ is one-one in $[1,\infty )$ but not in $(-\infty ,\infty )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\frac{x^{2}+2x+1}{(x^{2}+1)}$

$\Rightarrow f^{'}(x)=\frac{(x^{2}+1)(2x+2)-(x^{2}+2x+1)(2x)}{(x^{2}+1)^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow f^{'}(x)=\frac{2-2x^{2}}{(x^{2}+1)^{2}}$

$=\frac{2(1+x)(1-x)}{(x^{2}+1)^{2}}$

$\therefore$ $f^{'}(x)=0$ at x = 1 and x = -1. So, x = 1 and x = -1 are point of maxima/minima.

Option A : $f(x)$ is many-one in $(-\infty ,-1)$.

As x = -1 is a point of maxima/minima. So it is a boundary point in the range $(-\infty ,-1)$. So, $f(x)$ is one-one in $(-\infty ,-1)$.

$\therefore$ Option A is incorrect.

Option B : $f(x)$ is one-one in $(-\infty ,\infty )$.

As, x = 1 and x = -1 are point of maxima/minima which is present inside the range $(-\infty ,\infty )$. So, $f(x)$ is many-one function in $(-\infty ,\infty )$.

$\therefore$ Option B is incorrect.

Option C : $f(x)$ is one-one in $[1,\infty )$ but not in $(-\infty ,\infty )$.

As x = 1 is a point of maxima/minima. So it is a boundary point in the range $[1,\infty )$. So, $f(x)$ is one-one in $[1,\infty )$.

As, x = 1 and x = -1 are point of maxima/minima which is present inside the range $(-\infty ,\infty )$. So, $f(x)$ is many-one function in $(-\infty ,\infty )$ .

$\therefore$ Option C is correct.

Option D : $f(x)$ is many-one in $(1,\infty )$.

As x = 1 is a point of maxima/minima. So it is a boundary point in the range $[1,\infty )$. So, $f(x)$ is one-one in $[1,\infty )$.

$\therefore$ Option D is incorrect.

Note :

Methods to Check One-One Function :

(i) If a function is one-one, any line parallel to $x$-axis cuts the graph of the function maximum at one point.

(ii) Any continuous function which is entirely increasing or decreasing (no maxima/minima is present) in whole domain will always be one-one function.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

Consider the following system of equations

$αx+2y+z=1$

$2αx+3y+z=1$

text: If the vectors $\vec{a}=λ\hat{i}+μ\hat{j}+4\widehat{k}$, $\vec{b}=-2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-2\widehat{k}$ and $\vec{c}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$ are coplanar and the projection of $\vec{a}$ on the vector $\vec{b}$ is $\sqrt{54}$ units, then the sum of all possible values of $λ+μ$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$⃗{a}=λ\hat{i}+μ\hat{j}+4\hat{k},⃗{b}=-2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-2\hat{k},⃗{c}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\hat{k}$

Now, $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b}=\sqrt{54}\Rightarrow \frac{-2λ+4μ-8}{\sqrt{24}}=\sqrt{54}$

$\Rightarrow -2λ+4μ-8=36$

$\Rightarrow 2μ-λ=22...(i)$

and $\left |\begin{array}{lll} λ & μ & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \end{array}\right |=0$

$10λ-2μ-56=0...(ii)$

By (i) & (ii) $λ=\frac{78}{9},μ=\frac{138}{9}$

$\therefore μ+λ=24$

text: Let $a_{1},a_{2},a_{3},...$ be a $GP$ of increasing positive numbers. If the product of fourth and sixth terms is 9 and the sum of fifth and seventh terms is 24, then $a_{1}a_{9}+a_{2}a_{4}a_{9}+a_{5}+a_{7}$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $r$ be the common ratio of the G.P

$\therefore a_{1}r^{3}\times a_{1}r^{5}=9$

$a_{1}^{2}r^{8}=9\Rightarrow a_{1}r^{4}=3$

And

$\begin{array}{ll} \quad a_{1}\left (r^{4}+r^{6}\right )=24 \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & 3\left (1+r^{2}\right )=24 \\  \\ \therefore  & r^{2}=7\text{and}a_{1}=\dfrac{3}{49} \end{array}$

Now

$\begin{array}{l} a_{1}a_{9}+a_{2}a_{4}a_{9}+a_{5}+a_{7} \\  \\ =a_{1}^{2}r^{8}+a_{1}^{3}r^{12}+24 \\  \\ =24+\dfrac{9}{7^{4}}\times 7^{4}+\dfrac{27}{7^{6}}\cdot 7^{6}=60 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Suppose $f$ is a function satisfying $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ for all $x,y\in N$ and $f(1)=\frac{1}{5}$. If $\sum\limits _{n=1}^{m}\frac{f(n)}{n(n+1)(n+2)}=\frac{1}{12}$, then $m$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because f(1)=\frac{1}{5}\therefore f(2)=f(1)+f(1)=\frac{2}{5}$

$f(2)=\frac{2}{5}f(3)=f(2)+f(1)=\frac{3}{5}$

$f(3)=\frac{3}{5}$

$\therefore \sum\limits _{n=1}^{m}\frac{f(n)}{n(n+1)(n+2)}$

$=\frac{1}{5}\sum\limits _{n=1}^{m}\left (\frac{1}{n+1}-\frac{1}{n+2}\right )$

$=\frac{1}{5}\left (\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{4}+\ldots .+\frac{1}{m+1}-\frac{1}{m+2}\right )$

$=\frac{1}{5}\left (\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{m+2}\right )=\frac{m}{10(m+2)}=\frac{1}{12}$

$\therefore m=10$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Let the coefficients of three consecutive terms in the binomial expansion of $(1+2x)^{n}$ be in the ratio 2 : 5 : 8. Then the coefficient of the term, which is in the middle of those three terms, is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{r}+1}={}^{\mathrm{n}}\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}}(2\mathrm{x})^{\mathrm{r}}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \dfrac{{}^{\mathrm{n}}\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}-1}(2)^{\mathrm{r}-1}}{{}^{\mathrm{n}}\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}}(2)^{\mathrm{r}}}=\dfrac{2}{5} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{\frac{n!}{(r-1)!(n-r+1)!}}{\frac{n!(2)}{r!(n-r)!}}=\dfrac{2}{5} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{\mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{n}-\mathrm{r}+1}=\dfrac{4}{5}\Rightarrow 5\mathrm{r}=4\mathrm{n}-4\mathrm{r}+4 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 9\mathrm{r}=4(\mathrm{n}+1)...(1) \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{{}^{n}C_{r}(2)^{\mathrm{r}}}{{}^{\mathrm{n}}\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}+1}(2)^{\mathrm{r}+1}}=\dfrac{5}{8} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{\frac{n!}{r!(n-r)!}}{\frac{n!}{(r+1)!(n-r-1)!}}=\dfrac{5}{4}\Rightarrow \dfrac{r+1}{n-r}=\dfrac{5}{4} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 4\mathrm{r}+4=5\mathrm{n}-5\mathrm{r}\Rightarrow 5\mathrm{n}-4=9\mathrm{r}...(2) \end{array}$

From (1) and (2)

$\Rightarrow 4\mathrm{n}+4=5\mathrm{n}-4\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=8$

$(1)\Rightarrow r=4$

so, coefficient of middle term is

${}^{8}\mathrm{C}_{4}2^{4}=16\times \frac{8\times 7\times 6\times 5}{4\times 3\times 2\times 1}=16\times 70=1120$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: If the co-efficient of $x^{9}$ in $\left (αx^{3}+\frac{1}{βx}\right )^{11}$ and the co-efficient of $x^{-9}$ in $\left (αx-\frac{1}{βx^{3}}\right )^{11}$ are equal, then $(αβ)^{2}$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Coefficient of $\mathrm{x}^{9}$ in $\left (αx^{3}+\frac{1}{βx}\right )^{11}={}^{11}C_{6}\cdot \frac{α^{5}}{β^{6}}$

$\because$ Both are equal

$\therefore {}^{11}C_{6}\cdot \frac{α^{5}}{β^{6}}=-{}^{11}C_{5}\cdot \frac{α^{6}}{β^{5}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{β}=-α$

$\Rightarrow αβ=-1$

$\Rightarrow (αβ)^{2}=1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Let $f:\mathrm{ℝ}\to \mathrm{ℝ}$ be a differentiable function that satisfies the relation $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)-1,\forall x,y\in \mathrm{ℝ}$. If $f^{'}(0)=2$, then $|f(-2)|$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)-1$

$\begin{array}{l} f^{'}(x)=\lim _{h\to 0}\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h} \\  \\ f^{'}(x)=\lim _{h\to 0}\dfrac{f(h)-f(0)}{h}=f^{'}(0)=2 \\  \\ f^{'}(x)=2\Rightarrow dy=2dx \\  \\ y=2x+C \\  \\ \mathrm{x}=0,\mathrm{y}=1,\mathrm{c}=1 \\  \\ \mathrm{y}=2\mathrm{x}+1 \\  \\ |f(-2)|=|-4+1|=|-3|=3 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: Let the co-ordinates of one vertex of $\Delta ABC$ be $A(0,2,α)$ and the other two vertices lie on the line $\frac{x+α}{5}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z+4}{3}$. For $α\in \mathrm{ℤ}$, if the area of $\Delta ABC$ is 21 sq. units and the line segment $BC$ has length $2\sqrt{21}$ units, then $α^{2}$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The point $(-α,1,-4)$ lies on the line, whose direction is $⃗{d}=5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ with $|⃗{d}|=\sqrt{38}$.

Since B and C lie on the line, the height of $\Delta ABC$ from A is the distance $h$ of A from the line:

$\frac{1}{2}\cdot BC\cdot h=21\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\sqrt{21}h=21\Rightarrow h=\sqrt{21}$

The vector from $(-α,1,-4)$ to A is $⃗{a}=α\hat{i}+\hat{j}+(α+4)\hat{k}$, and

$⃗{a}\times ⃗{d}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ α & 1 & α+4 \\ 5 & 2 & 3 \end{array}\right |=-(2α+5)\hat{i}+(2α+20)\hat{j}+(2α-5)\hat{k}$

Using $h=\dfrac{|⃗{a}\times ⃗{d}|}{|⃗{d}|}=\sqrt{21}$:

$(2α+5)^{2}+(2α+20)^{2}+(2α-5)^{2}=21\times 38=798$

$12α^{2}+80α+450=798\Rightarrow 3α^{2}+20α-87=0\Rightarrow (α-3)(3α+29)=0$

Since $α\in \mathrm{ℤ}$, $α=3$, so $α^{2}=9$.

Hence, the answer is 9.
